borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed development would result in a poor standard of accommodation for future occupiers, by reason of inadequate natural light to the bedroom and the provision of external amenity space that is not private, being directly overlooked by the public highway thus resulting in an unacceptable living environment. As such, the proposal would be contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies D6 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DMD1 of the LBBD Local Plan (September 2024)DCLG Technical Housing Standards (nationally described space standard) (DCLG, March 2015).

The proposed dwelling, by reason of its siting forward of the established building line, continues to result in a prominent and incongruous form of development that disrupts the established pattern and undermines the character of the area. The design is of poor quality lacking articulation and with a scale, form, and appearance more akin to an ancillary outbuilding than a standalone dwelling, and fails to respond positively to the surrounding built context. As such, the proposal would be contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies&nbsp;D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy SP2 and DMD1 of the LBBD Local Plan (September 2024)

The application fails to demonstrate compliance with statutory biodiversity requirements and the mitigation hierarchy. The exemption from Biodiversity Net Gain is not justified, the submitted metrics are inconsistent, and insufficient detail has been provided on mitigation, enhancement, and long‑term management. As such, the proposal would be contrary to:Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990
description:
Construction of a detached single storey 1x bed
dwelling with associated car parking, private amenity space, and cycle storage
